judgments.justification: “four of five” and “decreased on KA” are wrong; both variants improved COMET on all five low-resource targets.
The passage does not report the language- and variant-specific low-resource BLEU pattern.
It reports the dynamic high-resource results but omits the contrasting mixed results for M-static.
“but not on BLEU” is false, and the passage omits that M-static, not dynamic, had the highest XCOMET.
It does not state that every RL configuration scored below supervised fine-tuning on every metric.
It reports lower values without FILTER/NN for only three metrics, omitting COMET.
“No statistical significance tests were reported” and differences “cannot be characterized as statistically reliable” accurately state the central reliability limitation.
The multiple training, reward, stopping, and evaluation roles of COMET-KIWI are not discussed.
“but not on BLEU” reverses the comparison: dynamic with FILTER/NN exceeded supervised BLEU, 14.47 versus 14.11.
“most low-resource pairs” and the exclusion of BN are wrong; both Method M variants improved COMET on every low-resource pair.
“but not on BN” is wrong, and the generic MR claim obscures M-static’s decrease versus M-dynamic’s slight improvement.
“M-dynamic improved both BLEU and COMET” on DE and ZH, while “M-static did not consistently improve,” correctly summarizes the contrast.
“highest scores on all four metrics” is false because M-static had higher XCOMET; “not on BLEU” is also false.
The passage does not compare every REINFORCE and PPO configuration directly with supervised fine-tuning across all metrics.
“scores were higher with them than without on all metrics” correctly reports increases in BLEU, KIWI, COMET, and XCOMET.
It does not mention seed averaging, standard deviations, significance tests, or statistical reliability.
It does not report COMET-KIWI’s roles in training, RL reward, early stopping, and evaluation.
“though not on BLEU” is wrong: dynamic with FILTER/NN beat supervised on BLEU as well as the other three metrics.
“four of five” is wrong because dynamic improved COMET on KA too, and the passage does not cover M-static.
“BLEU gains were mixed” for dynamic does not report the required language-specific pattern for both Method M variants.
The dynamic improvements on DE and ZH are reported, but the mixed M-static results are omitted.
“but not on BLEU” is false, and the passage omits M-static’s highest XCOMET result.
It does not report that all RL configurations were below supervised fine-tuning on all four metrics.
The removal comparison covers BLEU, COMET-KIWI, and XCOMET but omits the COMET increase from adding FILTER/NN.
“No statistical significance tests were reported” and differences “cannot be characterized as statistically reliable” correctly convey the package’s limitation.
No statement describes COMET-KIWI’s overlapping methodological and evaluation roles.
“but not on BLEU” contradicts the table, where dynamic with FILTER/NN exceeded supervised BLEU, 14.47 to 14.11.
The list “AZ, MN, MR, and KA” wrongly omits BN and does not establish that both variants improved every low-resource target.
The BLEU summary omits BN and conflates variants, failing to report M-static’s MR decrease and M-dynamic’s slight MR increase.
“M-dynamic improved both BLEU and COMET” on DE and ZH, whereas M-static “did not consistently improve,” correctly captures the finding.
“highest scores on all four metrics” misstates XCOMET leadership, and “not on BLEU” wrongly denies dynamic’s advantage over supervised.
It does not state that every REINFORCE and PPO row trailed supervised fine-tuning on all metrics.
“scores were higher with them than without on all metrics” accurately covers all four reported increases.
“no significance tests were reported” correctly communicates the central reason statistical reliability is not established.
The passage does not explain COMET-KIWI’s use as training signal, reward, early-stopping criterion, and evaluation metric.
“though not on BLEU” is false because dynamic with FILTER/NN exceeded supervised on all four metrics, including BLEU.
